title: Versunkener Apfelkuchen
subtitle: German sunken apple cake
excerpt: A simple vanilla sponge batter has apple quarters pressed into the top before baking. The apples sink slightly as the cake bakes, giving the cake its name. This is a classic German home cake -- modest, fragrant, and very good.
sourceNotes: Versunkener Apfelkuchen means 'sunken apple cake'. The apple quarters are pressed into the batter and sink slightly as the cake bakes. It is a simple German home cake found in every bakery and on every grandmother's table in autumn.

content.text: Versunkener Apfelkuchen is one of the simplest and most satisfying cakes in German baking. The batter comes together quickly and the apples do the decorating for you. At its best eaten slightly warm with a spoonful of whipped cream.

items.prepNote: zest only -- also peel and quarter 3 large eating apples to press into the top

content.text: Heat oven to 180°C. Grease and line a 23cm round cake tin.
Beat butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder, salt, lemon zest, and vanilla until just combined.
Spread batter into the prepared tin.
Peel and quarter 3 large eating apples. Press each quarter cut-side down into the batter in a fan pattern, spacing evenly.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted into the sponge (not the apple) comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes then turn out.

items.symptom: Centre is still wet after 45 minutes
items.fix: Return to the oven for 10 more minutes and test again with a skewer.

content.text: Germany and Austria. Often served with a dusting of icing sugar and a spoonful of whipped cream. A Sunday afternoon staple throughout autumn, when eating apples are at their best.
